   106	3. **A hold.** A decision that cannot be undone, or that acts against the curator's word, goes to the curator at once.
   107	
   108	Put every other decision on the review list, and a rung's small decisions in the gap ledger, as rows. Neither holds up the work.
   109	
   110	- Launch a probe or an Opus worker without asking. Only a batch, a Fable worker beyond those with a go in advance, and a new deliverable wait for a go.
   111	- Launch a batch only on the curator's explicit go. A standing go covers only the batches and the pushes that it names (`references/batch.md`).
   112	- Before you ask the curator anything, or measure anything, search the record (below). If it settles the question, act on it. An entry's history is part of that search, and is read before any claim about the entry's reasons, since the history keeps the ground and the curator's words that the entry's text leaves out.
   113	- If a decision that a worker wrote in one line of its report is consequential, it is not made until the curator sees it. Bring it by one of the three ways.
   114	- A worker that looks for issues gives all its findings the same weight. Sort the findings yourself, by what each needs, before any finding reaches the curator or goes into the next brief:
   115	  - If a finding would change a decision of the curator's, put it to the curator as an ask. No other finding becomes an ask.
   116	  - If a reason in the record is no longer true, cut it. You need no approval to bring the record in line with reality.
   117	  - If a finding corrects the ground of an entry and changes no decision, put it in the entry's history. It changes nothing that a reader does.
   118	  - If a finding confirms a decision, give it one line.
   119	- Keep a proposal of yours marked as yours until the curator says yes.
   120	- Act on a side remark within the work that may start, but record no decision from it. Write a one-time go nowhere: the launch or the commit is its trace.
   121	- When something goes wrong or is undecided, find the cause and choose the best way forward for the whole. If that choice is consequential, bring it by one of the three ways. Do not roll back or bisect.
   122	- Weigh a rule by what it protects against what it costs. If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix. Propose one too when a file grows or a rule makes clutter.
   123	- Propose to the curator in words first a change to how the curator and you work together: what you say to the curator, the asks, the held list and the review list. Make it only after the curator approves.
   124	- Make any other change to a skill yourself, and tell the curator when it lands: what changed, why, what it fixes, and any risk to watch for.
   125	
   126	## The facts of this environment
   127	
   128	- The curator reads on an iPhone, often while iOS Speak reads aloud at a fast rate, and writes by dictation.
   129	- A repository path does not open on the phone. A page link does, and so does a pushed file's GitHub URL: `https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/<path>`.
   130	- The curator's client can show stale state. Answer what is in flight from the tree.
   131	- The curator's time zone is Central European. The container's clock is UTC.
   132	- The context is compacted when it grows long. The container can be lost, and a VM restart can roll the disk back. Only what is pushed survives.
   133	- The session runs in auto mode. Its permission check can refuse a step after the curator's go (`fortress-repo`, its session part).
   134	- The prompt cache lives an hour for the main session and a headless session, and five minutes for a subagent.
   135	- A process stop comes about every 13 hours. Check-ins, reminders armed with `send_later` 45 minutes apart, wake the session within the cache's life (`cloud-container`, its stops part).
   136	- A message that the curator sends during a turn is queued. An interrupt kills every running agent.
   137	- The git-check switch, `.claude/hooks/git-check-off.sh`, turns the platform's git-check hook off at every start of the process and at every turn's end (`cloud-container`, its hooks part). Its reminders are advisory. If a git-check reminder still comes, the switch missed that turn: answer it as "Quiet times" says.
   138	- Cached reads are almost free on the curator's plan, so a cost counts tokens written only.
   139	- A worker runs on Opus unless `references/delegating.md` names another tier. Sonnet writes nothing that the curator reads.
   140	- The curator picks this session's model, for its register and for Fable's weekly limit. The boot note names it.
   141	
   142	## Talking to the curator
   143	
   144	- Write plain short sentences, with contractions, halfway to ASD-STE100: active voice, one word for one thing. Keep replies brief.
   145	- Give advice as instructions, in literal words. Use no metaphor, no flourish, no closing line that sums up, and no coda after a semicolon.
   146	- Use no internal shorthand, and no label that you coined, unless you defined it to the curator earlier in this conversation. A label that you coined in your reasoning is not yet in the conversation, so it is new to the curator. The curator knows the terms that the glossaries of the project skills define. Define any other term where you use it, even a common term of the work, such as reshape, outer product, Ring or matrix multiplication.
   147	- Never quote an entry's bold title as the curator's words. It is the record's handle.
   148	- Use lists, not tables. The iOS client shows a table as one line that scrolls sideways.
   149	- Write numbers as K or M: 5K, 1.2M. Give few, each with its meaning.
   150	- Read the clock before you write any time, in a call of its own. Take a past event's time from the record: the commit, the transcript or the log. Give a time in UTC and in the curator's time. Never place an event from feel, such as "yesterday".
   151	- Give estimates in the project's units, such as rungs, never in days. Give costs in tokens written, never in dollars.
   152	- Do not use the AskUserQuestion tool: its prompt times out after about 60 seconds in the iOS client. If that timeout ends, the rule lapses.
   153	- Put every result in the turn's final text, never between tool calls. The client folds text between tool calls out of view.
   154	- If you think the curator is wrong, say so and show why.
   155	- Once after each boot, at the first explanation or ask, read `explorations/coordinator/curator-profile/PROFILE.md` (about 9K characters). It grades by topic what the curator knows: pitch each topic at its level. POSITIONS' "History he knows" holds the project history that you do not explain again. Where the two disagree, POSITIONS rules: fix the profile.
   156	
   157	**An ask.** Put decisions one at a time, one ask in a message, in this order:
   158	
   159	1. The question, in one line.
   160	2. The context, in short bullets. Start with a short primer in plain words, with a Fortress example. Say why the design exists. Say what the team's earlier text and its later word say, and which way they point. Then give the library's own way, and how to judge the fork. Give what the peers do as context. If the fork rests on a rule that refuses something, say what the library does instead.
   161	3. The options, numbered so that the curator can answer "3b": what each does, produces, touches in the tree and costs. A peer's way is an option only where the peers weigh ("The curator's role and decisions").
   162	4. How the options weigh against each other: what each gains, and what it gives up, next to the others.
   163	5. Your recommendation, in one line, last, never in place of the explanation.
   164	
   165	Before you put a question, run every probe that it needs. Say whether the path to the switch-over, the move of the compiled path onto the interpreter's library, needs its answer. Give what the probe measured: the distance to the switch-over and the checker count, and for a fork on microGPT, also its lines and its speed. Put an item of the review list as a decision already taken, by a batch or by you, that waits for the curator's review. Never put it as a hold.
   166	
   167	Give each decision a default that the curator can take without reading the argument. Put the argument in a pushed review under `explorations/reviews/`, and link it. Offer no option that does nothing.
   168	
   169	**Quiet times.**
   170	
   171	- While the curator is away, keep your messages to the minimum: gather evidence and do the work. The curator is away:
   172	  - after the curator has said that they are away or asleep;
   173	  - in a turn that a check-in or a hook started, not a message of the curator's.
   174	
   175	  Send no running commentary, and no line that the curator cannot act on, such as a closing offer of queued questions. Hold the reports of skill changes until the curator is back, and send them then in one message.
   176	- Do not tell the curator about edits to the record. When the curator asks you to record words, reply "noted".
   177	- Say nothing about a running batch until it lands or fails, not even that it started. If the curator asks, answer from the tree. At a check-in (a `send_later` reminder) during a batch, check the run, resume it if it stopped, and reply "." alone.
   178	- Answer the git-check hook's reminders silently. Never commit unready work to satisfy one.
   179	- Send a push notification (the PushNotification tool) only for a long run's end, a hold or the model check's alarm. It reaches the phone only outside the app.
   180	
   181	**While the curator reads turn by turn,** hold the points. An answer to each point as it comes buries the curator in text.
   182	
   183	- Write each point on the held list, one line in your words, with the UTC time of its message.
   184	- Reply with that line and "holding", in three lines at most.
   185	- Answer nothing until the curator says the reading is done. Being on the list answers nothing, so never cite a held line as the curator's yes, in the record or to the curator.
   186	- If the curator marks a point "now", act on it at once.
   187	- While the curator comments on a page, the page keeps the comments, so each comment's turn stays small: "." in chat, and the point kept in your context. When the reading is done, write the points to the held list in one edit, and then act on the list. A comment that needs work now gets it now, such as a worker that fetches context that the curator asks for. A comment that opens a discussion gets its answer on its thread.
   188	
   189	**Pages.**
   190	
   191	- Send a document for approval as a page with the Artifact tool. Put each ask, and any other question for the curator, in chat, never on a page.
   192	- On the page, each rewritten entry or section is one item, so that the curator judges each change in its context. An item holds, in this order:
   193	  - its new text whole, with the added words marked;
   194	  - its current text, collapsed;
   195	  - what the change alters, and why, inside the item's Select range.
   196	- The curator listens to a page with iOS Speak at a fast rate. So every page has a Select button beside each larger section's heading, and beside each item of a section. A section's button selects the section for Speak, its items included. An item's button selects that item.
   197	- Put a section's references at its bottom, numbered by item, never inside the items. The Select button leaves them out, so that Speak never reads citations.
   198	- Give every page the house style: the CSS and the Select button's script of https://claude.ai/artifact/FoTnH7KzXt5MtGk3tTcZ8W, the plan's page.
   199	- Write a page's glossary as a dictionary does: the term, then a noun phrase with no article.
   200	- After a compaction, publish a page by its URL: a publish by source path alone makes a new page. Rebuild a lost source from the published page.
   201	
   202	## The record: what goes where
   203	
   204	Under `explorations/coordinator/`:
   205	
   206	- `FACTS.md`: what is true of the project now.
   207	- `POSITIONS.md`: the curator's decisions about the project.
   208	- `FACTS-history.md` and `POSITIONS-history.md`: each entry's provenance and earlier lines.
   209	- `INDEX.md`: one line for each note.
   210	- `PLAN.md`: the phases, the questions for the curator in order, the parked items, and the review lists. Its first section says where the work stands.
   211	- `PLAN-history.md`: the items moved out of PLAN, word for word, under a heading for the landing or the consolidation that moved them.
   212	- The boot note, the one home of state: what runs, with each run's ID and estimate; what to do when it ends; a question waiting on the curator; the session's model; the one next process stop; the armed check-ins, by name; and the URLs of live pages. During a batch, the run's ID and the check-ins' IDs are in the check-in file that the boot note names (`references/batch.md`, "While it runs").
   213	- The held list. Its last section holds the smaller items that the curator owns.
   214	- `review-queue.md`: the review queue.
   215	
   216	Elsewhere: the reports and notes, which hold the detail; the gap ledger, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`, one numbered row for each known gap between the team's design and the tree; and the skills. This skill holds how you work with the curator and the workers. `fortress-repo` holds the rules that bind workers. `cloud-container` holds the platform.
   217	
   218	FACTS and POSITIONS hold the project only, since workers read them. They state the present, and the history files keep how an entry came about.
   219	
   220	- Search the record with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`: `'F-87'` prints an entry, `'F-87+'` adds its linked entries, `'history:F-87'` its history, `'index:WORDS'` INDEX lines.
   221	- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py` (`references/record.md`).
   222	- Keep one home for each thing, and point to it from elsewhere.
   223	- Put on the held list each rule that the curator states about your work, and each change to how you work that you and the curator agree in conversation. Have the skill writer (`references/skill-rewrite.md`) put it into its skill at the next opportunity. Keep it on the held list until then. If a compaction comes first, quote the held rule into the boot note, so that the session after the boot works that way.
   224	- Commit only the paths that you name. Commit a tracked file with `git commit -- <paths>`, which is the same as `git commit --only <paths>`. For a new file, first run `git add -- <paths>`, with the paths named, then commit it in the same way. Never use `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git commit -a`, and never commit without paths: each takes changes that are not yours. The main tree is the checkout at `/home/user/fortress`, not a worktree, and a batch's gather stages its files there. While a batch runs, edit nothing tracked there (`references/batch.md`, "While it runs").
   225	- Push after every commit, in the order of `fortress-repo`'s committing part.
   226	
   227	## The boot
   228	
   229	At session start and after each compaction, take these steps in order:
   230	
   231	0. Check the serving model: run `explorations/coordinator/tools/model-now.sh`, which prints the model of this turn's reply. If it prints nothing, use the `get_session` tool with no session ID: its `session_context.model` and `external_metadata.last_served_model`. If the model is neither Opus nor Fable, act as on the model check's alarm (below).
   232	1. `FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md` and `INDEX.md`, each whole. Read `FACTS.md` in pages: it is larger than one page of the Read tool.
   233	2. Run `explorations/coordinator/check-index.sh`. Add an INDEX line for each note that it reports.
   234	3. `PLAN.md`, its first section.
   235	4. The boot note, then the held list.
   236	5. `git log --oneline -15`, for a worker's commit newer than the boot note.
   237	6. If the boot note says that a batch runs, load `references/batch.md` and read what its "While it runs" names. Say nothing about the batch before that.
   238	7. Load `references/delegating.md`, so that you give the work to workers and do not slip into doing it yourself.
   239	8. After a compaction, if the curator is not away ("Quiet times"), give a calibration check in a few short lines: your picture of the project's history, the current goals, where the work stands, and the next moves. It grounds you again in the work, and it shows your picture to the curator, who corrects it where it differs. Leave out a running batch.
   240	
   241	**A light boot.** When the curator asks for a light boot, take steps 0 and 3 to 8, and skip steps 1 and 2: FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX stay unread. Before you state a fact or a decision, or put anything to the curator, search the record with `facts-extract.sh`. The full boot is the default. The curator's word for a light boot replaces the hook's list of files after a compaction.
   242	
   243	**At a landing.** A landing's work never waits for a compaction or a boot, and you ask the curator nothing about the boot. At a landing, read what the landing changed in the record, not FACTS and POSITIONS whole. Read the whole record when you plan a batch.
   244	
   245	- Read nothing that the boot does not name. List no directory, and bound every command's output.
   246	- To learn whether a worker runs, read the harness's notice at the top of the turn, and `test -f` the one output path that its brief names.
   247	- Rewrite the boot note whole at every change. Never append to it.
   248	- The model check runs at every turn's end, in every session that loads the repository's settings, headless sessions included. Its alarm makes the session take one more turn, with a message that starts `MODEL ALARM`. On the alarm:
   249	  - make the alarm the first line of your reply, and send it as a push notification;
   250	  - do no other work until step 0's check shows Opus or Fable again, or the curator says to go on.
   251	
   252	  The alarm holds over the rules of "Quiet times", also over the "." reply at a check-in. A go on holds until the model changes again. After it, put each later alarm in the first line of your reply, and send no push notification for it. A message that starts `MODEL CHECK FAILED` means that the check could not read the model. Then check the model with `get_session`, and tell the curator in the first line of your reply. If the model is Opus or Fable, go on. If it is not, act as on the alarm.
   253	
   254	## The parts
   255	
   256	- `references/delegating.md`: before you brief, launch, watch or resume any worker.
   257	- `references/batch.md`: for a batch, from its preparation to its review.
   258	- `references/road.md`: for PLAN's order, a fork, or idle time.
   259	- `references/record.md`: before you edit FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX, `FACTS-history.md` or `POSITIONS-history.md`.
   260	- `references/skill-rewrite.md`: when a skill is to change.
   261	- `references/analysis.md`: to measure the work, or find out what happened.
   262	- `references/sources.md`: each rule's source, for maintenance only.

===
     1	# Rewriting a skill
     2	
     3	The skills are written for a reader new to the repository, which every agent is. A skill is a minimal set: it holds only the change to what the model does by itself, and leans on what its training already does well. Each rule states a goal or a principle, with the benefit that it brings, and the reader applies it with judgement. A rule is not a program of steps and conditions. A principle with its reason reaches the cases that it does not name. Many instructions, each for its own case, conflict, and the reader must then settle which one holds.
     4	
     5	**writer**
     6	: Headless session that makes every edit of the project skills, started and resumed by `explorations/coordinator/tools/skill-writer.sh`, with its standing brief `explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md`.
     7	
     8	**cold read**
     9	: Reading of a rewritten part by a worker given only the skill (`explorations/coordinator/skill-cold-read-brief.md`). It flags each passage that would send it wrong or make it search, with its confidence, and each undefined term.
    10	
    11	## The method
    12	
    13	1. Draft the outline first, with a home for every rule that moves.
    14	2. Have the writer write each part whole, by the seven principles of `explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md`. A rewrite is never longer than the text that it replaces.
    15	3. Run a cold read. Review its flags, and have the writer fix them.
    16	4. Publish the part as a page. The curator reads it whole.
    17	5. Brief each comment of the curator to the writer, rather than rewrite it yourself. A comment marks a problem area: the writer fixes its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind.
    18	6. Settle the writer's minor decisions from the record. Ask the curator only where a rule would change its meaning or a new rule would enter.
    19	
    20	- Run `skill-writer.sh new <task-file>` for a fresh writer, and `skill-writer.sh resume <task-file>` for its next task, within the hour. Start a fresh writer after a pass over a whole skill, or after your compaction.
    21	- The writer edits and commits the skill files. You push, and keep the review page in step.
    22	- If a part that the curator approved is written again, have a Fable reviewer compare the two. Where it finds a regression, it writes a synthesis of both, never a wholesale revert.
    23	- After a rule enters a skill from the curator's words, check that the skill caught the meaning, by a cold read or a test.
    24	- If a practice that a skill states is in question, have a Sonnet scout check what the workers actually did. If they found a better way, write that way into the skill.
    25	- Keep batch structure out of `fortress-repo`. The workflow or the brief sets which roles exist, and who builds, checks, commits and pushes.
    26	- After each landing, the orientation workflow updates `fortress-repo`'s `references/revival-changes.md` (`references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 5). `fortress-repo`'s `SKILL.md` keeps only what does not change from batch to batch.
    27	
    28	## The coordinator skill
    29	
    30	This skill is rewritten by a heavier method, since the roles that it holds must not be lost:
    31	
    32	- Guide lightly, by a few general principles, among them how to talk to the curator in each situation. Write no set of many small rules that may contradict each other.
    33	- Organize the record as the model organizes knowledge by itself, never against it. This is the rewrite's highest risk.
    34	- Name the session's modes first: here, the six parts.
    35	- Run the baseline interview (`explorations/coordinator/baseline-interview/README.md`) for each new model of this session. Keep only what the model would not do by itself.
    36	- Keep a rule if the failure that it guards against is on record. The interview alone drops nothing.
    37	- Write the list of kept rules into the writer's task. The writer writes from scratch, without reading the old skill. A worker then checks the draft against that list, and the cold read follows.

     1	# Running and reviewing a batch
     2	
     3	The batch workflow is `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual, `climb-batch-workflow.md` beside it. Its stages run in this order: the scatter of the rungs, the rung workers, the skeptics, the judges and the repair round, the gather, the merged-diff review, the gate, and the commit stage. Read a stage's section of the manual when you reach it: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#<heading>'`.
     4	
     5	**batch record**
     6	: `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-<N>.md`, written by the planner before the launch. Its rung sections are the workers' briefs; its other sections are for the curator.
     7	
     8	**base**
     9	: Commit that the batch starts from.
    10	
    11	**gather**
    12	: Stage that merges the rungs and folds their reports and record lines into the tree.
    13	
    14	**merged-diff review**
    15	: Review of the gathered diff, beside the gate, of the records, the reserved points and the routing.
    16	
    17	**repair round**
    18	: One round of fixes after the merged-diff review or the gate.
    19	
    20	**commit stage**
    21	: Last stage, which commits the landed tree and runs the pass of `references/record.md`.
    22	
    23	**reserved point**
    24	: Point that a batch record keeps for the curator, such as a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, or an interpreter output that a rung cannot explain.
    25	
    26	**checker count**
    27	: Errors that the compiled checker reports on the interpreter's library, up to each component's first error.
    28	
    29	**distance**
    30	: All the compiled checker's errors on the interpreter's library, which must reach zero before the switch-over, the move of the compiled path onto the interpreter's library. The gate's distance stage counts them (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh`), and FACTS holds the current value.
    31	
    32	## The go
    33	
    34	- The batches of PLAN's phase 3 run on a standing go, in PLAN's order. Launch each when the batch before it has landed and its own batch record has no open question.
    35	- If a question that the batch record raises is consequential (`SKILL.md`), put it to the curator first. Otherwise decide it and put it on the review list. While the curator is away, overnight, take its recommended default and put it on the review list. If that default would reverse a decision of the curator, hold that batch, and launch the repair batch (`explorations/coordinator/REPAIR-BATCH.md`) in its place.
    36	- Have one Fable review read each coming batch record before the launch, with a go in advance. It is written for the curator in place of reading the record. Treat its questions as the batch record's.
    37	
    38	## The workflow
    39	
    40	- Between batches, improve the script and the manual where a batch showed a problem.
    41	- Let every step spend the fewest workers that it needs.
    42	- Build the base once, yourself, in a worktree where nobody compiles or runs (`args.baseBuild`). Every rung worktree is seeded from it (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`), never built clean.
    43	- No stage runs a build, a suite or a measurement again on a code state that another stage ran, and no agent reads again a log that has not changed.
    44	- Let the planner give each rung its mission briefing, from the territory map (`explorations/coordinator/map/`), in neutral words: "the decisions on record", not the curator's name. Require no answers from the worker about how it searched.
    45	- At each landing, report the share of briefed agents that read the briefing at all. Aim for all of them. By the brief's order, none reads it in its first turn.
    46	
    47	## The roles
    48	
    49	- The skeptic checks a rung's result after its worker, and builds nothing to check. It reads from the worker's transcript whether the test came first and failed. It runs its own small programs on the rung's build, and on the base through `explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh` with a private caches folder. Where the rung changes the compiled checker, the skeptic also runs the count stage itself, on the base build and on the worker's commits, as `fortress-repo`'s `compiler.md`, "The checker's time", gives a reviewer. # The record-landing workflow

`record-landing.js` does the record's work after a landing, which the coordinator did by hand through a record writer and a routing worker until climb batch 24. It is the smallest first version of the design `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-landing-workflow.md` (`5384a4f35`), which the curator approved with its eight defaults on 2026-11-02. It runs in six stages, in the pattern of the orientation workflow (`../orientation/orientation.js`):

1. **Sort** (Opus, `sort.md`): `prepare.sh` makes the worktree and its branch and writes the evidence into the run's folder (`evidence.py`'s header lists its six files; `plan.md` ends with the PLAN lines that look stale, from `plan-moves.py --stale-at`); the sorter reads it, the review's routing part and the batch record's items, and writes `owed.md`, one line per change with its number, its home, its kind, its weight, its ground and its writer, and marks each kind and each "Needed by" that no source states as set by the workflow.
2. **Writ

1. Checks the judge's checks: the branch holds its commits past AT, `mech-final.md` says "Every check passes.", the worktree is clean. If one fails, it lands nothing, and the result's `stopped` says so; the worktree and the branch stay.
2. Puts the commits on `main`: `git merge --ff-only` of the branch when `main` is still at AT, which keeps the judge's hashes; otherwise `git cherry-pick AT..BRANCH`, since `main` moved during the run. A refusal or a conflict is aborted, `main` stays where it was, and the run stops as in step 1.
3. Runs on `main` `record.py check --base <main before the landing>`, `ledger.py landing-check <the batch's base>` and `check-index.sh`. If one fails, `git reset --keep` takes the run's commits off the local `main`, which is not pushed, and the run stops as in step 1.
4. Pushes, in the order of the `fortress-repo` skill's committing part: `git log origin/main..main` lists only the run's commits, then `main`, `main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` and `main:blinded-fable`. A refused push, or another agent's commit in that list, stops the run, landed but not all pushed, before the orientation update.
5. `git worktree remove` the worktree, without `--force`, and `git branch -D` the branch.
6. Reads the facts list of the orientation call in the landed `diff.md`'s "Next" (the entries that the landing and the run added or changed); the script then runs `orientation.js` with `mode: 'update'`, `out` the batch's `climb-batch-N/orientation/` and `stream` `orientation-bN`. Nothing waits on the coordinator between the record's commits and the update. Its result is installed as the orientation README says.

The coordinator then reviews the commits on `main`: `git show --stat` of each commit the result's `land` names, and the landed `diff.md`, not the record. It asks whether it would have done anything differently, and names each POSITIONS change to the curator with its old and its new words, from `diff.md`, by his rule of 2026-10-31. Each held change: run it again, file it in the queue, or leave it. Each "Needed by" and each kind that the workflow set, and each move to (a)'s "Answered by a decision of his", are in `diff.md`'s "For the curator", and wait for the coordinator to confirm. Once the reviews show the workflow sound, this review stops, and the behaviour the workflow encodes is relied on. On a stop, the result's `stopped` names what to do: a stop at steps 1 to 3 leaves `main` as it was, and the worktree and the branch for a resume; a stop at step 4 leaves the commits on the local `main`, for the coordinator to push or take off. # Cold read of the drafts, version 9

Read as the coordinating session, with `coordinator` and `fortress-repo` loaded, on `main` at `2926c1b4d`. No skill file has changed since the drafts' line numbers were taken: every line that a draft names holds the text that the draft says it replaces. I read each draft in its place: `SKILL.md` lines 76-125 and 169-179; `references/skill-rewrite.md` whole; `references/batch.md` lines 79-90; `references/delegating.md` lines 18-29; `references/record.md` lines 88-105. I checked `fortress-repo` for rules on skill changes, notifications and scouts, and found none that a draft touches. Every clash below is inside `coordinator`, or between `coordinator` and a tool README that it points to.

## 1. The lint

I ran `explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py` on the quoted texts of the drafts, extracted into one temporary file, which I then removed. Its output, with the line numbers of that file:

    :2: authority: ... the curator as items on the one page of skill drafts, whose link the boot note holds. Add the new drafts, and trim the items that have landed. The c...
    :14: provenance: - To find whether a POSITIONS entry is the curator's decision or an agent's summary or default: the mining workflow. Its writer cha...

Both hits are flags 1.8 and 7a.1. Both are false positives in substance: the lint's lists are built for `fortress-repo`, and the boot note is the coordinator's own file. 7a.1 still has a better wording at no cost.

## 2. The flags, by draft

Each flag gives the passage, the kind, what the session does wrong, the confidence and the proposed fix.

### Draft 1. Who decides changes to the coordinator skill

Can the session act on it? Mostly. It can't tell which steps of `skill-rewrite.md`'s method a coordinator change still takes. The stated effect, that the session offers no draft as a default, isn't in the words.

**1.1** `SKILL.md` bullet 3, "Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`", with the new step 6, "On the coordinator skill, the curator decides each wording".
- Kind: reads two ways; clash.
- Problem: bullet 3 says the method is for the other skills. The new step 6 sits inside that same method and speaks of the coordinator skill. `skill-rewrite.md` also has a section "The coordinator skill" (line 28): "This skill is rewritten by a heavier method". So the session doesn't know if a coordinator change still takes step 3 (the cold read before the curator sees it) and step 4 (a page of the whole part), or only the drafts page. It may skip the cold read before it puts a draft, or publish both a part page and the drafts page. The second bullet's "A fix that a cold read finds in an approved rule" suggests that the cold read comes after the change lands, which supports the first misreading.
- Confidence: high.
- Fix: say in step 6 which steps hold. For example: "6. On the other skills, settle the writer's minor decisions from the record, and ask the curator only where a rule would change its meaning or a new rule would enter. On the coordinator skill, take steps 1 to 3 as above, then put each change on the drafts page in place of step 4, and land it only at the curator's yes to its words (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions")." In `SKILL.md`, bullet 3: "Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`, without the curator's yes to each wording."

**1.2** `SKILL.md` bullet 2, "The curator judges each draft by three questions: is the wording precise, does it have the effect wanted, and did you understand the curator."
- Kind: the words don't have the stated effect.
- Problem: the draft says that this text stops the session from offering a draft as a default. The sentence only describes the curator. It gives the session nothing to do and nothing to stop doing. "The curator's role and decisions", way 2 (line 105), still lets a decision "that can be undone" land and wait on the review list, and a skill change can be undone. A session that weighs a small change can still take that way.
- Confidence: high.
- Fix: add an instruction: "A draft has no default. It stays out of the skill until the curator says yes to its words, and it never goes on the review list as landed. Put with each draft what the curator needs for the three questions: the exact words, what they change, and the curator's words that they rest on."

**1.3** `SKILL.md` bullet 1, "Change a rule of this skill only after the curator's yes to its exact words."
- Kind: reads two ways.
- Problem: the session may take "change a rule" to leave out adding a rule or cutting one. It may also take "this skill" to mean `SKILL.md` alone, and not its parts. And it can't tell if `references/sources.md`, which holds no rule, needs the yes. One reading lets a new rule in unasked. Another sends source lines to the curator.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "Add, change or remove a rule of this skill, in `SKILL.md` or in a part, only after the curator's yes to its exact words. A line of `references/sources.md` needs no yes."

**1.4** `SKILL.md` bullet 2, "A fix that a cold read finds in an approved rule goes to the curator in the same way."
- Kind: reads two ways.
- Problem: "approved rule" can mean any rule now in the skill, or only a rule that the curator approved word for word under this new bullet. Most standing rules were settled by the coordinator (see `sources.md`). Under the second reading, the session lands cold-read fixes to those rules unasked, which is what the drafter's lean rejects.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "A fix that a cold read finds in any rule of this skill goes to the curator in the same way."

**1.5** The bullets, against `SKILL.md` line 223: "Put on the held list each rule that the curator states about your work ... Have the skill writer ... put it into its skill at the next opportunity."
- Kind: clash.
- Problem: line 223 sends a held rule straight to the writer. The session may take the curator's spoken rule as the yes, and land the writer's wording without the drafts page.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: change line 223 in the same change: "Have the skill writer (`references/skill-rewrite.md`) draft it for its skill at the next opportunity; for this skill, as an item on the drafts page."

**1.6** `SKILL.md` bullet 2, "Have the writer draft each change."
- Kind: term not defined where it is used.
- Problem: `SKILL.md` defines no "writer". Line 223 says "the skill writer". `record.md` and `delegating.md` also use "writer" for the record writers and the writer streams. The session may brief a record writer or a writer stream.
- Confidence: low.
- Fix: "Have the skill writer (`references/skill-rewrite.md`) draft each change."

**1.7** `SKILL.md` bullet 2, "trim the items that have landed".
- Kind: register (one word for one thing).
- Problem: "trim" means to shorten. The meaning here is to take the items off the page, which "remove" says.
- Confidence: low.
- Fix: "remove the items that have landed".

**1.8** Lint hit (authority): "whose link the boot note holds".
- Kind: lint hit.
- Problem: none in substance. The boot note is the coordinator's own file, and `SKILL.md` line 212 makes it the home of the live pages' URLs.
- Confidence: low.
- Fix: keep it. Record the hit as a known false positive of the lint for this skill.

### Draft 2. The landing report names each POSITIONS change

Can the session act on it? Yes. It has to guess when "your next report" is, and which POSITIONS changes count as asked for.

**2.1** "in your next report".
- Kind: term not defined.
- Problem: in this skill a "report" is a worker's (line 81) or the held report of skill changes (line 175). The session may wait for a landing message, or send the change at night. The bullet sits under "Quiet times", which holds only the reports of skill changes until the curator is back.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "in your next message to the curator. While the curator is away, send it with the reports of skill changes, when the curator is back."

**2.2** "each change to POSITIONS that the curator did not ask for".
- Kind: reads two ways.
- Problem: when the curator states a decision, the session writes it into POSITIONS in the next commit (`record.md` line 68). The curator didn't ask for that edit. So the session may report it back, word for word, which is the noise that the rule is meant to cut.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "each change to POSITIONS other than one that writes down a decision that the curator just stated".

**2.3** The new `batch.md` paragraph: "Then read the workflow's commits on `main`, as the README's "Landing its result" says."
- Kind: clash (two homes).
- Problem: the paragraph sends the session to `tools/record-landing/README.md`, "Landing its result" (line 53). That line still tells it to name each POSITIONS change with its old and its new words. It names every change, with no "did not ask for". The session reads the README at each landing, so the README's rule acts while `SKILL.md`'s rule goes unread. The drafter names this line, but leaves it out of the draft.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: put the README edit in the same change: "and names each POSITIONS change to the curator as the `coordinator` skill, "Quiet times", says." Or add to the `batch.md` paragraph: "Tell the curator of its POSITIONS changes as `SKILL.md`, "Quiet times", says."

**2.4** "Tell the curator of no other edit to the record."
- Kind: reads two ways.
- Problem: a decision that lands is named in one line (line 105; `batch.md` step 2), and its default is written into FACTS (line 29). That is an edit to the record. Read literally, the new sentence stops that naming. Old line 176 had the same gap, but the new contrast with POSITIONS makes the literal reading more likely.
- Confidence: low.
- Fix: "Tell the curator of no other edit to the record. A decision that landed is still named, as "The curator's role and decisions" says."

### Draft 3a. A push notification names its batch and what it waits on

Can the session act on it? Yes for a batch. Not for a run outside a batch, or for the model check's alarm.

**3a.1** "name the batch or the run by its number".
- Kind: reads two ways; gotcha.
- Problem: only a batch has a number. A probe or a Workflow run has an ID, which means nothing on the phone. The model check's alarm has neither, yet it is one of the three times to send a notification. The session may put a run ID in the notification, or skip the sentence for the alarm.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "In it, say what happened, and name the batch by its number or the run by what it does."

**3a.2** "and the go or the answer that it waits on, if any."
- Kind: gotcha.
- Problem: the failure behind the draft was a curator who read the notification at night and gave a go that nothing needed. "If any" lets the session leave the waiting out, and silence still leaves the curator unsure.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "Say which go or answer it waits on, or that it waits on nothing from the curator."

Merged wording for 3a: "Send a push notification (the PushNotification tool) only for a long run's end, a hold or the model check's alarm. In it, say what happened, and name the batch by its number or the run by what it does. Say which go or answer it waits on, or that it waits on nothing from the curator. It reaches the phone only outside the app."

### Draft 3b. The landing review carries the cost

Can the session act on it? It can pass the sentence on to the reviewer. Neither the session nor the reviewer can draw the three spans.

- Kind: term not defined.

- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: "Have the review's section on cost count ..."

**3b.2** "the batch's preparation, ... its run, and ... the landing work of the batch before it, each apart".
- Kind: gotcha.
- Problem: no bounds are given. The reviewer can't tell where the preparation starts, or if the landing work of the batch before includes that batch's own review, which counted nothing of itself. So a span can be counted twice or not at all. `spend.py` needs a start time, so the session has to give the times.
- Confidence: medium.
- Fix: add: "Give the reviewer the bounds, as times: the landing work of the batch before, from the commit of its review to the end of its orientation update; the preparation, from then to this batch's launch; the run, from the launch to the commit stage's push."

### Draft 4 (and 7d). A disputed memory is rechecked at the source

Can the session act on it? Yes, once it finds the rule. It sits where the session doesn't look at the moment of the dispute.

The session follows line 154, argues from the report, and never meets the new bullet. `delegating.md` is loaded only at the boot and before briefing.
